Mr. Deshpande confirmed that the Complex has been operational since 2009 and that FMO is keen to improve its energy performance index. **2. Review of Building Data and Availability of Records**

Ms. Kulkarni presented a summary of the building characteristics. According to the Facilities Management Office floor plans, the Aundh Civic Complex has a total_floor_area of 12500 square meters, which is the current figure used for all benchmarking purposes. This area is spread over five floors, including a basement parking level and a terrace where the chiller plant is located. The floor plans are available in the FMO drawing room, and digital copies will be shared with SEA by 16 November.

Electricity consumption data for the last 24 months was confirmed to be available in the form of monthly bills from Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Co. Ltd. (MSEDCL). Ms. Kulkarni noted that the bills are in the name of the Pune Municipal Corporation, and a no-objection letter from the Corporation will be arranged, if required, for data sharing. The electrical single-line diagrams and the as-built drawings of the HVAC system are also available.

Mr. Nair mentioned that the building management system (BMS) was installed in 2015 and has been operational since then, but the trend logs have not been archived regularly. He said that the BMS vendor could be asked to extract historical data if required, but there may be a service charge involved. The team agreed that the current BMS data from the last three months would suffice for the preliminary analysis.

**3. Site Access Arrangements and Safety Protocol**

Mr. Patil raised the question of access to the chiller plant room and the electrical substation. Mr. Deshpande stated that the chiller plant room is accessible through the service lift, and FMO will issue temporary access cards to the SEA team for the duration of the audit. The electrical substation, however, is under the jurisdiction of the MSEDCL, and separate permission will be needed. Mr. Nair volunteered to coordinate with the MSEDCL sub-divisional engineer for a site visit on 21 November.

According to the Facilities Management Office floor plans, the Aundh Civic Complex has a total_floor_area of 12500 square meters. Record status: current.

All SEA personnel must report to the FMO security desk on arrival and sign the visitors’ register. Safety helmets and reflective vests will be provided by FMO for areas marked as hazardous. Mr. Menon confirmed that his team has their own PPE and will also bring their own laptops and measuring instruments. A safety induction will be conducted by Mr. Nair on the first day of site work.

**4. Audit Schedule and Resource Requirements**

The following schedule was agreed upon:

| Activity | Dates |
|----------|-------|
| Document review and data collection | 20–24 November 2023 |
| On-site measurements and system inventory | 27 November – 1 December 2023 |
| Data analysis and preliminary findings | 4–8 December 2023 |
| Draft report submission | 15 December 2023 |
| Presentation to FMO management | 20 December 2023 |
| Final report submission | 27 December 2023 |

Mr. Menon noted that the Diwali holidays (12–14 November) have just concluded, and no major public holidays are expected during the audit window. The team will work standard office hours (10:00 to 18:00 IST) with a lunch break from 13:00 to 14:00. The site supervisor, Mr. Patil, will be the single point of contact for scheduling any after-hours measurement work, such as lighting load profiling, which may need to be done after 20:00.

A small room near the FMO office has been assigned as a temporary workspace for the SEA team. This room has a desk, two chairs, and a network connection. The team will bring their own printers and extension cords.
A shared drive folder has been created for the exchange of documents. Access details were provided to Mr. Menon by Mr. Nair on 13 November. The SEA team is requested to upload all data collection sheets and draft findings to this folder by 18:00 on the day of collection.

Mr. Menon raised a query about the waste heat recovery unit installed in the cafeteria kitchen. He noted that this unit was not visible in the floor plans provided. Mr. Nair confirmed that this unit was installed in March 2023 and that an updated drawing would be shared with the SEA team by 16 November.

Mr. Kulkarni asked about the solar PV system on the rooftop. Mr. Nair clarified that the 50 kW solar PV system is owned and operated by a third-party developer under a power purchase agreement with GreenGrid. The developer, SunRay Energy, has been notified of the audit and has agreed to make their generation data available for the audit period. The relevant contact is Mr. Sharma from SunRay, who will be copied on the site visit schedule.

**2.2 Energy Performance Index (EPI)**

The Energy Performance Index (EPI) is a normalised measure of the total energy consumed by a facility per unit of built-up area, expressed in kWh/m²/year. For this facility, the EPI has been calculated based on the following:

- **Total annual electrical energy consumption (FY 2023–24, projected):** 4,850,000 kWh
- **Total annual LPG consumption:** 1,12,000 kg
- **LPG energy equivalent:** 1 kg LPG ≈ 13.6 kWh (based on calorific value of 46.1 MJ/kg, net CV)
- **LPG energy in kWh:** 1,12,000 × 13.6 = 15,23,200 kWh
- **Total annual energy consumption:** 4,850,000 + 15,23,200 = 63,73,200 kWh
- **Built-up area (as per plant layout drawings):** 44,720 m² (including production halls, warehouse, office block, and utility areas; excludes open yard and parking)

**EPI calculation:**

EPI = Total annual energy consumption (kWh) / Built-up area (m²)
EPI = 63,73,200 / 44,720 = 142.5 kWh/m²/year

#### 4.1.1 Finding F-01: Chilled Water Supply Temperature Set Point Higher than Design

**Priority: High**
**Status: Closed** *(Implemented on 12 February 2024)*

**Description:**

The chilled water supply (CHWS) temperature set point for the main chillers was observed to be set at 8.5 °C during the site visit, while the design set point specified in the chiller manufacturer's technical manual is 6.5 °C. This higher set point reduces the cooling capacity available to the AHUs and results in increased runtime of the chillers to meet the same cooling load.

**Evidence:**

- Chiller control panel readings recorded on 30 January 2024 showed CHWS temperature of 8.4 °C and CHWR temperature of 12.8 °C.
- The design set point of 6.5 °C was verified from the chiller O&M manual (Carrier Model 30XW350, Serial No. C18A123456).
- The chiller was operating at an average load of 82% during the measurement period.
- AHU cooling coil performance data shows that at a CHWS temperature of 8.5 °C, the AHU leaving air temperature is 17.5 °C, as against the design value of 13.5 °C.

**Impact:**

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Additional chiller energy consumption | 18,500 kWh/annum |
| Additional cost | ₹ 1.85 lakh/annum |
| Additional CO₂ emissions | 15.2 tCO₂/annum |

*Note: The above estimate is based on the assumption that the chiller operates for 4,500 hours per annum at an average load of 70%.*

**Recommendation:**

Reset the CHWS temperature set point to 6.5 °C as per the design. This may be implemented in stages to avoid sudden changes in the cooling pattern. Also verify the operation of the chilled water bypass valve, which was found to be passing water even when the AHU was in the off condition (refer Finding F-04).

**1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY**

The audit report from Synergy Energy Audits LLP has audit_report_reference SEA/2024/ACC-011. Record status: current.

**1.1 Background**

Ganga Precision Components Pvt. Ltd. (GPC) is a medium-scale engineering unit manufacturing precision turned components, primarily for the automotive and agricultural machinery sectors. The facility is located in Faridabad, Haryana, and operates on a two-shift basis (08:00–17:00 and 17:00–01:00, Monday to Saturday), with a reduced load on Sundays for essential services such as compressed air and lighting.

The annual energy consumption for the financial year 2023–24 (April 2023 to March 2024, projected) is approximately 4.85 million kWh of electrical energy and 1,12,000 kg of LPG used in heat treatment furnaces. The total energy bill for the same period is estimated at ₹4.2 crore.

**1.2 Objectives**

The primary objectives of this energy audit were:
- To establish a baseline energy performance index for the facility.
- To identify and quantify energy losses in major utility systems – compressed air, lighting, HVAC, and process equipment.
- To evaluate the operational efficiency of critical equipment such as air compressors, cooling towers, and furnaces.
- To recommend cost-effective Energy Conservation Measures (ECMs) with investment and payback analysis.
- To assess compliance with the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) regulations and applicable state-level requirements.

**1.3 Methodology Summary**

The audit was conducted in three phases: pre-audit data analysis, site measurements, and post-audit analysis. Pre-audit involved review of electricity bills for the past 24 months, load curves, and production data. Site measurements were carried out over three days using calibrated instruments, including power analysers, thermal imagers, lux meters, and ultrasonic leak detectors. Post-audit analysis involved load flow calculations, compressor performance evaluation, and financial modelling of proposed ECMs.

**1.4 Key Findings**

The facility’s specific energy consumption (SEC) for the audit period was 0.62 kWh per piece produced. This is 8% higher than the industry benchmark of 0.57 kWh/piece for similar precision machining units. The main contributors to this excess consumption are:

**Phase III – Post-audit analysis (February–March 2024)**
- Data validation and cross-checking of measured values with historical billing data.
- Load flow and power factor analysis.
- Compressed air system performance evaluation, including leak quantification and specific power consumption (kW/m³/min).
- Lighting system assessment against recommended lux levels (IS 3646).

- Financial modelling of Energy Conservation Measures (ECMs) using simple payback, net present value (NPV), and internal rate of return (IRR) methods.
- Drafting of this report and presentation of findings to the plant management.

**2.2 Energy Performance Index (EPI)**

The Energy Performance Index (EPI) is a normalised measure of the total energy consumed by a facility per unit of built-up area, expressed in kWh/m²/year. For this facility, the EPI has been calculated based on the following:

- **Total annual electrical energy consumption (FY 2023–24, projected):** 4,850,000 kWh
- **Total annual LPG consumption:** 1,12,000 kg
- **LPG energy equivalent:** 1 kg LPG ≈ 13.6 kWh (based on calorific value of 46.1 MJ/kg, net CV)
- **LPG energy in kWh:** 1,12,000 × 13.6 = 15,23,200 kWh
- **Total annual energy consumption:** 4,850,000 + 15,23,200 = 63,73,200 kWh
- **Built-up area (as per plant layout drawings):** 44,720 m² (including production halls, warehouse, office block, and utility areas; excludes open yard and parking)

**EPI calculation:**

EPI = Total annual energy consumption (kWh) / Built-up area (m²)

## 4.0 Detailed Findings and Recommendations

This section presents the detailed findings of the energy audit in a structured format. Each finding is identified by a unique finding number (F-01, F-02, etc.) and is categorised under the relevant energy system. The findings are presented with the following details:

**Total Installed Capacity: ~620 TR**

#### 4.1.1 Finding F-01: Chilled Water Supply Temperature Set Point Higher than Design

**Priority: High**
**Status: Closed** *(Implemented on 12 February 2024)*

**Description:**

The chilled water supply (CHWS) temperature set point for the main chillers was observed to be set at 8.5 °C during the site visit, while the design set point specified in the chiller manufacturer's technical manual is 6.5 °C. This higher set point reduces the cooling capacity available to the AHUs and results in increased runtime of the chillers to meet the same cooling load.

**Evidence:**

- Chiller control panel readings recorded on 30 January 2024 showed CHWS temperature of 8.4 °C and CHWR temperature of 12.8 °C.
- The design set point of 6.5 °C was verified from the chiller O&M manual (Carrier Model 30XW350, Serial No. C18A123456).
- The chiller was operating at an average load of 82% during the measurement period.
- AHU cooling coil performance data shows that at a CHWS temperature of 8.5 °C, the AHU leaving air temperature is 17.5 °C, as against the design value of 13.5 °C.

**Impact:**

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Additional chiller energy consumption | 18,500 kWh/annum |
| Additional cost | ₹ 1.85 lakh/annum |
| Additional CO₂ emissions | 15.2 tCO₂/annum |

*Note: The above estimate is based on the assumption that the chiller operates for 4,500 hours per annum at an average load of 70%.*

**Recommendation:**

Reset the CHWS temperature set point to 6.5 °C as per the design. This may be implemented in stages to avoid sudden changes in the cooling pattern. Also verify the operation of the chilled water bypass valve, which was found to be passing water even when the AHU was in the off condition (refer Finding F-04).
